en: The Banaue Rice Terraces utilize natural mountain slopes as giant inclined planes, reducing the physical effort needed to transport water and agricultural crops.
The deep, rough treads of Philippine jeepney tires increase friction with the road to prevent the vehicle from slipping during heavy tropical rains.
Galileo Galilei reportedly dropped two spheres of different masses from the Leaning Tower of Pisa to prove gravity accelerates all falling objects equally.
The Chuo Shinkansen in Japan uses superconducting magnets to levitate the train above the tracks, eliminating wheel friction for ultra-fast magnetic travel.
The Angat Hydroelectric Dam in Bulacan converts the kinetic energy of flowing water into electrical energy to power millions of Philippine homes.
The James Webb Space Telescope uses 18 hexagonal mirrors coated in microscopic gold to efficiently reflect infrared light from distant, ancient galaxies.
The sperm whale produces clicks reaching 230 decibels, making it the loudest animal on Earth, to navigate and hunt prey using echolocation.
The Tiwi Geothermal Power Plant in Albay harnesses the Earth's internal heat from magma to boil water and spin electricity-generating turbines.
The Voltaic pile, invented by Alessandro Volta in 1800, was the first electrical battery, generating current through chemical reactions between zinc and copper discs.
The Venus flytrap plant stores chemical energy in its leaves, which rapidly converts to kinetic energy when its sensitive trigger hairs are touched.
Philippine National Railways trains require a large unbalanced force from their diesel engines to overcome inertia and start moving forward from a station.
The International Space Station uses massive ammonia-cooled radiators to dissipate excess heat generated by its electronics into space through thermal radiation.
